sermon.title: A Phenomenal Event
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “A Phenomenal Event,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins with Isaiah 10:1-3 and says leaders who make unrighteous laws will face God’s judgment. He then teaches Isaiah 11, the seven spirits of the Holy Spirit, the judgment of the Branch from Jesse, and the phenomenal event of the wolf dwelling with the lamb, which he links to the remnant, Isaiah 65 and the nations rallying to Jesus. He ends with praise in that day in Isaiah 12.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Isaiah 11:6” when he reads “They will neither hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain,” which is Isaiah 11:9. The captions give “Isaiah 10:es 1-3” and “Isaiah 11:es 1 and 2,” read here as verses 1 through 3 and 1 and 2, and “a chute” in Isaiah 11:1, read as “a shoot.” The captions garble some names that are corrected to the Bible spellings because the passage is clear (Baal in Romans 11:4, Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5, Arctic tern); the captions spell Osteen several ways (Ostein, Olstein), read here as Osteen. A few words are shown as [unclear] and not guessed. He names many real people and groups: two presidents, Oprah Winfrey, Rick Warren, Joel Osteen, the Pope, Martin Luther’s thesis, a man called Mr. Barnes, a restaurant protest, and the Republican and Democratic parties; he says Oprah is “living with a man in sexual immorality,” says he has two presidents on video saying the Bible is not a book of truth but a book of faith, quotes Rick Warren on national television, and says the Pope has declared for homosexual unions. These are his own statements about real people and have not been checked here. He also speaks about homosexuality as a crime, capital punishment, jobs shipped overseas, welfare, Mexico’s military and evolution, all as his own opinions and kept as spoken. His factual claims (a million jobs shipped overseas every year, an Arctic tern flying 40,000 miles to go 12,000, animals eating only plants for “over 1,600 years,” where the apostles traveled) are his own and have not been checked here.

He says the church fell away like Israel, and that the restoration since the Reformation produced denominations, but in that day people will look to Jesus Christ, not a denomination or leader.

Hallelujah. Okay. All right. Um now remember the early church did not reach the whole world. They didn’t even know there was another world out there. The early church, the apostles, only went to India. Up here, just north of the Black Sea, over to Spain. Some say they went to Britain. I can’t find any record of that in anything I researched.

chunks.short_answer: He says the early church did not know the full world, and that knowledge increases in the last days only as God gives it. Amen. But that’s the way we’re programmed in America today. See, everything’s cool. I’m a Catholic man. Even if I mess up, they give me the death rites. I’m in. Hallelujah. So, we got this lack of knowledge in the early church. Could it possibly be we don’t have the knowledge we think we have in our generation? That this big God we serve is really a big God and is going to do a big thing because heaven, the Bible says, has a multitude up there that can’t be numbered. faqs.question: What does he say is the name of the Messiah in Isaiah 11:1?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus came through the bloodline of Jesse, David and Judah, and that his name in the Bible is called the Branch, a name we never use.

scriptures.text_nkjv: There shall come forth a Rod from the stem of Jesse, And a Branch shall grow out of his roots. The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him, The Spirit of wisdom and understanding, The Spirit of counsel and might, The Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.

faqs.question: Does he say the Holy Ghost is God?
faqs.answer: He says the Holy Ghost is a prominent member of God, he is God, and that God is Jesus and Jesus is God. He says he does not understand why the church argues about the baptism of the Holy Ghost.

scriptures.text_nkjv: There shall come forth a Rod from the stem of Jesse, And a Branch shall grow out of his roots. The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him, The Spirit of wisdom and understanding, The Spirit of counsel and might, The Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.

faqs.question: Does he say the Holy Ghost is limited to tongues or prophecy?
faqs.answer: He says we want to limit him to just tongues or prophecy or education, but being full of the Holy Ghost means you have the whole thing, as a glass that is full is not a quarter full.

faqs.question: What does he say we must do to receive the Holy Ghost?
faqs.answer: He says all he can do is preach it, and you have to reach out and get it and pursue it, and that he highly recommends the Holy Ghost to people.

faqs.question: What does he say the holy mountain is?
faqs.answer: He says the holy mountain is the church, where there is unity and a lack of war, and that the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.

faqs.question: What does he say the "second time" in Isaiah 11 means?
faqs.answer: He says if there is a second time there had to be a first time, and that the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the remnant, the people who are left from the four quarters of the earth.

scriptures.text_nkjv: It shall come to pass in that day That the Lord shall set His hand again the second time To recover the remnant of His people who are left, From Assyria and Egypt, From Pathros and Cush, From Elam and Shinar, From Hamath and the islands of the sea. He will set up a banner for the nations, And will assemble the outcasts of Israel, And gather together the dispersed of Judah From the four corners of the earth. faqs.question: Can someone who rejects Jesus be part of the remnant?
faqs.answer: He says no: if an atheist or a Muslim rejects Jesus it disqualifies him from being the remnant, because once you have heard the gospel the rules change, and those who have not believed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ are condemned already.

faqs.question: How long does he say animals ate only plants?
faqs.answer: He says there was a period of over 1,600 years where the lion ate straw, and all animals ate plants until after the flood, when they ate meat.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you. I have given you all things, even as the green herbs.

faqs.question: How much of the world does he say the early apostles reached?
faqs.answer: He says the early church did not reach the whole world and did not know there was another world out there, and that the apostles went to places such as India, Spain, Italy, Egypt, Libya, Arabia and Assyria, and he could not find a record of them going to Britain.

faqs.question: What does he say about the many denominations?
faqs.answer: He says God started restoration and we keep building another group, another denomination, until in our generation there are new ones. He says that in that day people will look to Jesus Christ, not a denomination or some leader.

faqs.question: What does the Arctic tern illustrate?
faqs.answer: He says the Arctic tern flies over 40,000 miles to go 12,000, which he compares to Christians zigzagging from church to church and preacher to preacher. He says our basic instinct should be going to the book and staying where we are, because God will meet us right where we are.

faqs.question: What does he say about music and singing in church?
faqs.answer: He says music and singing is vitally important in the church and should come from the spirit back to God, anointed of God, not just going through motions. He says God ordained it to bring his glory, touch and change people’s lives and teach them his ways, not to entertain them.
